In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of precession on the search sensitivity is a combination of the effects of the three possible apparent precession cone orientations.

the effect of neglect of precession on the search sensitivity depends on the binary parameters, and on the orientation of the binary with respect to the observer, in a way that is not easy to quantify, but that can be estimated by our fitting-factor calculation.
neglecting precession in the sensitive band can reduce the sensitivity to spinning binaries by at most a few percent for most viewing geometries, but by up to 20% for the worst-case scenario.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effect of neglect of precession in searches for spinning binaries is not as large as might have been expected, but that it can be significant for some viewing geometries.

for black hole--black hole and black hole--neuron star binaries with significant spins, non-precessing templates are expected to have fitting factors less than 1, and that the best possible fitting factors are typically 0.7-0.9.

for a given precessing binary system, we can determine whether the non-spinning waveform is a good template or not, without needing to compute the precession cone geometry, and without needing any knowledge of the binary parameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the constant precession-cone approximation is an excellent approximation for ground-based detectors, and can be used to predict the best possible fitting-factor in a non-precessing search for a given precessing waveform.
